title: Backend+client byte-fetch endpoints for Posekit source-image and OpenPose artifact display
origin: MT-014 de-scaffolding honest blockers (2026-07-02): the frontend posekit viewports now decode+display real bytes and bind to real keypoints, but no endpoint returns the raw bytes at runtime, so the left viewport shows the explicit empty state and the right renders openpose_json keypoints rather than the literal exported PNG pixels.

scope.summary: Add a backend route + frontend backend_client method to fetch raw bytes so the Posekit split view displays real pixels at runtime: (1) source-image bytes for PoseRig.source_asset_id / pose_source_ref (DAM/ckc_client asset-bytes endpoint) -> feeds the left source viewport (set_pose_source_image_bytes); (2) artifact-content bytes for the backend OpenPose export (png_artifact_ref) -> lets the right viewport render the literal exported PNG instead of re-rasterizing keypoints. Async fetch wiring on tab open / after export.
acceptance_criteria: AC1: A backend route (in api/atelier.rs or the DAM/ArtifactStore API) returns raw source-asset bytes for a source_asset_id/pose_source_ref, and a frontend backend_client method calls it; the left posekit viewport shows the decoded real image at runtime (not the empty state) when a source is set. Runtime-proven.

AC2: A backend/artifact route returns the exported OpenPose PNG bytes for png_artifact_ref; the right viewport can render the literal exported PNG (artifact://) at runtime, matching the backend render_posekit_openpose_png output. Runtime-proven.
AC3: Async fetch is wired (on tab open / after export) without blocking the UI; failures show explicit error state (HBR-QUIET headless, no fake).
AC4: PostgreSQL/EventLedger + ArtifactStore authority (no SQLite); Argus-inspectable; UserManual updated. No scaffolding.
AC5: This closes the MT-014 left-viewport empty-state and right-viewport keypoints-vs-PNG limitations.

hbr_obligations_note: HBR-INT (ArtifactStore/EventLedger byte fetch), HBR-VIS (Argus-inspect the loaded image/PNG), HBR-QUIET (async non-blocking, explicit error state), HBR-MAN (UserManual).

lifecycle.claim_recovery_reason: Status recovery: legacy RFV contract lacked lifecycle.claimed_by; Kernel Builder inspected current MT state and accepts implementer-side handoff responsibility without claiming validator PASS/FAIL.

legacy_rfv_evidence.summary: Committed 9902d7b0 (source-asset byte-fetch core). Runtime-proven: backend atelier_media_asset_bytes_route_returns_exact_stored_source_bytes (managed PG, exact bytes + 404 fail-closed); frontend posekit_source_viewport_displays_real_decoded_image + no-spurious-fetch guard + failure-empty-state. Posekit left viewport loads the real image. Follow-up increment: artifact-PNG-fetch so the right viewport shows the literal exported PNG.
legacy_rfv_evidence.note: Evidence summary copied into the MT contract for implementer-side checklist recovery only; this is not an official validator verdict.

validation_v1.basis: AC1 committed and proven; AC2 unimplemented (split to uncommitted MT-050).
validation_v1.fail_report: MT-043 is committed (9902d7b0): AC1 (source-asset byte route + set_pose_source_image_bytes + managed-PG exact-byte test + frontend real-PNG decode) is real and proven. But AC2 (and AC5-right) — the /atelier/posekit/openpose-png/bytes artifact route and the literal-PNG right-viewport render — live only in the uncommitted working tree (split-off MT-050). The contract still lists AC2 as a hard criterion and was never re-scoped, so an unimplemented committed acceptance criterion = FAIL_V1.
validation_v1.remediation_plan: Either: (a) commit MT-050 (which carries AC2/AC5-right) and re-validate MT-043+MT-050 together; OR (b) formally re-scope AC2 and AC5-right out of MT-043's contract into MT-050 (Orchestrator/operator decision) so MT-043's remaining ACs stand alone. Prefer (a).
